take: Falling Treasury yields set the tone: the US 10-year yield eased 6 bps to 5.24%, and Reuters credited that pullback for the equity rebound, with the S&P 500 up 0.19% and the Russell 2000 up 0.35%. Tech led US sectors with a 1.05% gain, helped by big jumps in Accenture (+15.8%) and Synopsys (+12.8%). Energy stocks also rose 1.95% even as WTI crude fell 3.71%, while health care (-1.32%) and communication (-0.93%) lagged. Europe picked up the calmer rates mood, with the DAX up 1.16% and the Stoxx 600 up 0.84%. Asia split: the Hang Seng fell 2.60% and the Nikkei slipped 0.94%, while the Kospi edged up 0.46%. Even with the bounce, the S&P 500 is still down 0.5% over five days, and PBS described bond yield swings rattling markets worldwide.
portfolio: The portfolio fell 0.13% while the S&P 500 gained 0.19%, mostly because Barclays (BCS, -2.60%), Apple (-0.81%), Alphabet (-1.70%) and VXUS (-0.59%, likely hurt by weakness in Hong Kong and Japan) outweighed gains in Salesforce (+3.10%, likely lifted with the broader software and IT services rally) and small-cap value fund AVUV (+1.13%). Over the past year the portfolio has matched the S&P 500's 14.2% return, but with slightly higher volatility (13.9% vs 13.0%) and a lower Sharpe ratio (0.74 vs 0.79).
watch: US futures point higher this morning, with the S&P 500 up 0.50% and the Nasdaq 100 up 0.73%, which would extend the rebound if yields stay contained.
Bond yields: the 10-year is still at 5.24%, and headlines flag ongoing swings that have moved stocks worldwide ahead of the October 28 Fed decision.
Barclays (BCS) reports on October 22, the first holding to report in an earnings run that includes GOOGL, AAPL, AMZN and DXCM in the last week of October.

take: US stocks closed last week on a firm note on Friday, with the Nasdaq up 1.19% and the S&P 500 up 0.73%, as tech (+1.01%) and consumer discretionary (+1.13%) led. That came even as the 10-year Treasury yield rose 4 bps to 5.28% and the VIX climbed 6.27% to 16.27, a partial reversal of the yield relief noted on Thursday. The gains were uneven inside tech: Teradyne rose 8.0% while Western Digital and Seagate each fell 10.2%, and Accenture gave back 6.3% after its big jump the session before. Japan carried the strongest momentum on Monday, with the Nikkei up 2.40% and 6.2% over five days. Europe was muted, with the Stoxx 600 up 0.31% and the DAX flat, while the Hang Seng added 0.28%. A firmer dollar pushed EUR/USD down 0.43%, and the S&P 500 is still down 0.3% over five days despite Friday's bounce.
portfolio: The portfolio rose 0.67% ($50), slightly behind the S&P 500's 0.73%. SCHG, VXUS and AAPL did most of the lifting, while losses in DexCom (-1.01%) and Salesforce (-0.84%), about $4 each, held it back.
watch: US futures are slightly lower (S&P 500 -0.09%, Nasdaq 100 -0.14%) as traders weigh soft jobs data against a 10-year yield sitting at 5.28%.
Reports that Anthropic is expected to IPO despite AI slowdown calls, a likely read on risk appetite for AI-linked names like GOOGL and AMZN.
The calendar is building toward Barclays (BCS) earnings on Oct 22, then the Fed decision and Alphabet earnings on Oct 28 and Apple, Amazon and DexCom on Oct 29.
deep_dive: The model puts Amazon at $58.14 a share against a $251.52 price, but the reverse DCF shows the price implies about 30.6% revenue growth a year for a decade, roughly double the 15.5% and 14.4% analyst estimates used for the first two years before the model fades growth to 2.5%. The bigger gap is likely margins: the model holds free cash flow at 5.2% of revenue for all ten years, while the market may be paying for that margin to widen meaningfully, and the high 12.11% discount rate, driven by a 5.28% risk-free rate, also keeps the value low, topping out near $73 even in the most generous sensitivity case. Treat this as one lens showing how much the price rests on profitability improving, not a verdict on the stock.

take: US stocks rose broadly on Monday even as the 10-year Treasury yield climbed another 3 bps to 5.31%, with the Nasdaq up 1.05% and the S&P 500 up 0.66%. Yields have now risen from 5.24% to 5.31% across the last three letters, yet the S&P 500 is up 1.2% over five days. Gains were spread widely: materials (+1.31%), communication (+1.17%) and energy (+1.00%) led, with energy rising even as WTI crude fell 2.05%. Japan again had the most momentum, with the Nikkei up 1.05% and 7.9% over five days as USD/JPY rose to 158.20. Europe followed the US higher (Stoxx 600 +0.73%, DAX +0.68%), the Hang Seng added 1.00% while the Kospi slipped 0.89%, and the 30.9% jump in Brazil's XP and 19.1% gain in Bradesco likely tie to the Reuters-reported Bolsonaro rally that pushed Brazil's exchange to a record.
portfolio: The portfolio gained 0.34%, trailing the S&P 500's 0.66%. SCHG (+1.05%, $14) and DXCM (+1.80%, $8) led, while CRM's 2.09% drop ($10) plus small declines in BCS and AAPL took back most of those gains.
watch: US futures point higher this morning, with the S&P 500 up 0.28% and the Nasdaq 100 up 0.40%, as the 10-year yield sits at 5.31%.
Barclays (BCS) reports earnings on Thursday Oct 22, the first holding on the calendar.
Wednesday Oct 28 brings the Fed rate decision alongside GOOGL earnings, followed on Oct 29 by AAPL, AMZN and DXCM, together about 31% of the portfolio.

take: The S&P 500 rose 0.58% on Tuesday to an all-time high, which headlines tied to continued bets on AI, and the 10-year Treasury yield eased 4 bps to 5.27% after climbing in recent sessions. Utilities led US sectors with a 2.98% jump, driven by power producers Talen Energy (+12.4%) and Constellation Energy (+12.2%), likely part of the same AI trade through expected electricity demand. Gains were narrow beneath the surface: the Russell 2000 fell 0.59% and health care slipped 0.17%, with genomics names Twist Bioscience (-18.6%) and 10x Genomics (-17.5%) among the biggest decliners. The mood did not carry overseas on Wednesday. The DAX fell 1.44%, the Stoxx 600 1.02% and the Kospi 1.98%, while the Nikkei lost 0.92% but is still up 4.9% over five days. US futures are lower, with the Nasdaq 100 down 0.57%, as one headline cited rising yields and another cited Iran mocking the US economy.
portfolio: The portfolio slipped 0.05% while the S&P 500 gained 0.58%, mainly because DexCom fell 4.04% ($-18) and Salesforce dropped 2.09% ($-10). Those losses outweighed gains in Amazon (+1.95%, $+10) and SCHG (+0.57%, $+8), and the portfolio has little exposure to the utilities rally that led the day.
watch: US futures point lower, with the Nasdaq 100 down 0.57% and the S&P 500 down 0.25%, after Tuesday's record close.
Barclays (BCS) reports earnings on Thursday Oct 22, the first holding to report this season.
The Fed rate decision on Wed Oct 28 lands the same day as Alphabet earnings, with Amazon and DexCom reporting the next day.

take: Geopolitics and oil likely set the tone heading into Thursday: WTI crude jumped 4.92% to $92.62 and US futures are lower (S&P 500 -0.56%, Nasdaq 100 -0.81%) as Benzinga reports the Pentagon is preparing for a potential military strike. On Wednesday the S&P 500 slipped 0.22% off record highs as the 10-year yield edged up 1 bp to 5.28%, which Reuters cited, but the damage was heavier in smaller and cyclical names, with the Russell 2000 down 1.31%, industrials down 2.18% and materials down 1.51%, while health care rose 1.03%. That is the second straight letter where small caps lagged a near-flat S&P, and the breadth signal in the regime still reads caution. Weakness spread overseas for a second day, with the Kospi down 2.62%, the Nikkei and Hang Seng each down about 1.4%, and the DAX down 1.04%. The Hang Seng is now off 3.4% over five days, and the VIX rose 5.77% to 15.95.
portfolio: The portfolio fell 0.28%, slightly worse than the S&P 500's 0.22% drop, mainly because of its non-US and small-cap holdings: BCS (-2.83%, $-17), VXUS (-1.18%, $-12) and AVUV (-1.11%, $-8) tracked the broad selloff abroad and in small caps. Gains in AAPL, AMZN and DXCM offset part of that loss.
watch: US futures are pointing lower (Nasdaq 100 -0.81%) with crude up 4.92% on the Pentagon strike report, so watch whether oil and the VIX keep climbing into the open.
BCS reports earnings on Oct 22 after falling 2.83% in Wednesday's session.
The Fed rate decision on Oct 28, with the 10-year yield still near 5.28%.

take: Chip stocks and a crude jump pulled US stocks lower on Thursday, Reuters reported. The Nasdaq fell 1.25% and the S&P 500 0.47% as tech dropped 1.79%, with Coherent (-9.6%), Astera Labs (-9.2%) and TTM Technologies (-8.3%) among the biggest decliners. Money rotated rather than fled: energy rose 2.97%, consumer staples rose 2.11% and financials rose 0.89%, while the 10-year yield fell 5 bps to 5.23% and gold gained 1.20%. The oil story carried over from the last letter's geopolitics, though WTI has since eased 0.80% to $90.76, and Friday trading turned firmer, with the Hang Seng up 1.79%, the DAX up 0.97% and the Stoxx 600 up 0.78%. One regime change: the breadth signal, flagged as caution in recent letters, now reads ok, which fits a day when the Russell 2000 held flat while big tech fell.
portfolio: The portfolio slipped just 0.09% against the S&P 500's 0.47% drop, as losses in SCHG (-1.22%) and Amazon (-2.25%), likely hit by the tech selloff, were nearly offset by gains in McDonald's (+2.61%), Apple (+1.11%), Salesforce (+1.44%) and AVUV (+0.84%). McDonald's gain likely rode the same defensive rotation that lifted consumer staples, and AVUV tracked the steadier small caps.
watch: US futures point to a rebound, with the Nasdaq 100 up 0.77% and the S&P 500 up 0.39%, so watch whether chip stocks recover after Thursday's slide.
Monday is Columbus Day and Indigenous Peoples Day. Headlines are asking whether markets will be open, so check before planning around that session.
Barclays (BCS) reports on October 22, the first holding to post earnings, ahead of the Fed decision and Alphabet results on October 28.

take: US stocks rose broadly on Friday, with the S&P 500 up 0.59% and the Nasdaq up 0.64%, even as a sharp telecom selloff (T-Mobile -13.3%, AT&T -9.8%, Millicom -9.6%) dragged communication down 1.51%, the weakest sector. Real estate (+1.86%) and health care (+1.58%) led, helped by Crown Castle (+15.6%), Moderna (+14.2%) and Humana (+11.6%). Europe followed the US higher on Monday (DAX +0.69%, FTSE 100 +0.65%) and the Hang Seng added 0.25%, but the Kospi fell another 3.65% and is now down 8.4% over five days, extending the Korean weakness seen in earlier letters. The breadth signal, which had just turned ok, is back to caution, fitting a week where the Russell 2000 slipped 0.9% while the S&P gained 1.2%. The VIX rose 4.38% to 15.49 and the 10-year yield held near 5.24%.
portfolio: The portfolio rose 0.36%, trailing the S&P 500's 0.59%, as Amazon's 3.29% jump and gains in SCHG and VXUS were partly offset by Apple's 1.11% drop and smaller losses in MCD and AVUV.
watch: US futures are close to flat (S&P 500 +0.06%, Nasdaq 100 -0.10%), so the open may not extend Friday's gains.
Barclays (BCS) reports Thursday Oct 22, the first earnings among your holdings.
The Fed decision and Alphabet earnings both land Wed Oct 28, followed by Amazon and DexCom on Oct 29.
deep_dive: At $229.13, Salesforce's price implies about 5.1% revenue growth a year for 10 years, well below the analyst estimates of 11.5% and 9.7% for the next two years that drive the model's $267 value. The model also holds the free cash flow margin flat at 32.8%, so any margin expansion would widen the gap, which suggests the market is skeptical of the growth rather than pricing in extra profitability. The result leans heavily on an 11.03% discount rate and a terminal value that is 48% of the total; at a 12% WACC and 1.5% terminal growth the value falls to $220, below the price, so treat this as one lens rather than a verdict.

take: A chip selloff that started in the US spread hard into Asia. The Kospi sank 5.46% on Tuesday and is now down 13.8% over five days, the steepest leg yet of the Korean slide tracked in recent letters, while the Nikkei lost 1.82%. On Monday US tech fell 1.22% and the Nasdaq 0.44%, led down by optical and chip names Cerebras (-10.7%), Semtech (-10.2%), Ciena (-10.0%) and Lumentum (-9.8%). The S&P 500 slipped only 0.06% because money again rotated toward energy (+1.43%), consumer staples (+1.17%) and communication (+0.97%), and an IMF warning that an AI share crash could threaten financial stability likely added to the caution. Europe held up on Tuesday, with the FTSE 100 up 0.59% and the Stoxx 600 up 0.36%, while WTI crude fell 2.04% to $91.83 and US futures point lower, led by the Nasdaq 100.
portfolio: The portfolio rose 0.28% while the S&P 500 slipped 0.06%, as gains in AAPL (+1.29%), CRM (+2.09%) and DXCM (+2.15%) added about $32 and more than offset declines in AMZN (-1.11%), SCHG (-0.41%) and VXUS (-0.45%). Its lighter tech weighting than the S&P (36%, 3 points under) helped on a day tech led the market down.
watch: Nasdaq 100 futures are down 0.59%, so watch whether the chip and optical selloff that hit the Kospi overnight extends into a third US session.
The IMF's warning on AI-driven stock risk, as Reuters notes markets are heading into earnings and economic data.
BCS reports earnings on Oct 22, the first holding to report this season.

take: Chip weakness and a firmer oil price again set the tone, with Reuters citing falling chipmakers as the Nasdaq slipped 0.15% on Tuesday while bank earnings began to roll in, leaving the S&P 500 nearly flat at -0.02%. The rotation seen in recent letters carried on: energy led US sectors with a 1.80% gain and is up 5.4% over five days as WTI crude rose 1.71% to $95.75, while tech is down 2.8% over the same stretch and health care fell 1.35% on the day. Smaller companies lagged again, with the Russell 2000 down 0.40%. Europe ignored the soft US tone on Wednesday, with the DAX up 0.62% and the Stoxx 600 up 0.55%, while Asia was roughly flat and the Kospi's 0.44% dip looks more like a pause in its slide, though it is still down 13.4% over five days.
portfolio: The portfolio rose 0.09% while the S&P 500 fell 0.02%, mainly because Salesforce (CRM) gained 1.75% and small-cap value fund AVUV and Barclays (BCS) added $4 and $3. These gains more than offset SCHG, which fell 0.41% alongside weaker growth and chip stocks, and Dexcom (DXCM), which dropped 1.00% on a day health care was the weakest US sector.
watch: US CPI inflation data and more big bank results, which Reuters says are lifting S&P 500 futures (+0.13%) even as Nasdaq 100 futures point 0.22% lower.
Whether oil keeps climbing after WTI's 1.71% rise to $95.75, extending energy's five-day lead over tech.
Barclays (BCS) reports on Thursday Oct 22, a read on European banks after the US bank results this week.

take: Hot US inflation data stirred rate-hike worries and deepened the tech selloff on Wednesday, Reuters reported, with the Nasdaq down 1.88% and the S&P 500 down 1.11% as tech fell 2.98%. AI infrastructure names took the hardest hits, including CoreWeave (-15.5%), DigitalOcean (-14.8%) and IREN (-12.2%), which fits the Guardian's note on fears over AI debt. Money again moved toward defensives: health care rose 2.53%, consumer staples 2.22% and gold 1.72%, while the 10-year yield slipped 3 bps to 5.19%. The chip weakness tracked in recent letters hit Asia hardest on Thursday, with the Kospi down 7.57% (18.4% over five days) and the Nikkei down 4.90%, as the FT reported that chipmakers tumbled. Europe held up better, with the FTSE 100 up 0.56% and the Stoxx 600 down only 0.28%.
portfolio: The portfolio fell 1.02%, slightly less than the S&P 500's 1.11%, as SCHG (-1.86%, $-25) and the big tech and growth names AMZN, GOOGL and DXCM led the losses. Gains in AAPL (+0.50%) and MCD (+1.06%) cushioned the drop, with MCD likely helped by the shift toward defensive stocks.
watch: Nasdaq 100 futures are down 1.33% against -0.33% for the S&P 500, so tech pressure looks set to continue at the open.
Whether the Kospi and Nikkei slide spills further into US chip and AI names.
BCS reports earnings next Thursday, October 22, ahead of the Fed decision on October 28.

take: A 10 bp drop in the 10-year Treasury yield to 5.09% helped a broad rally on Thursday that left out tech. The Russell 2000 rose 1.38% and the S&P 500 0.33%, while the Nasdaq managed only 0.08% as tech slipped 0.65%, extending its five-day loss to 4.3%. The rotation seen all week continued, with health care up 1.86%, materials 1.79% and consumer discretionary 1.71%, while chip and hardware names such as Vicor (-10.4%), Semtech (-10.0%) and Hewlett Packard Enterprise (-7.1%) fell again. Energy was the weakest sector, down 1.58%, as WTI crude fell 2.07% to $95.94. Asia bounced on Friday after its chip-driven slide, with the Kospi up 2.05% (still down 14.5% over five days) and the Nikkei up 1.39%, while the Hang Seng's 0.52% gain likely drew some support from China's new selling curbs and buybacks, and the DAX added 1.03%.
portfolio: The portfolio gained 0.87%, well ahead of the S&P 500's 0.33%, mostly thanks to Salesforce (+4.57%, $+22) and an unusual 5.08% jump in DexCom ($+21), helped by McDonald's (+1.76%) and small-cap value fund AVUV (+1.05%) as the rally broadened beyond big tech. Apple (-0.28%) was the only holding that fell, in line with the soft tech tape.
watch: US futures are mixed, with the S&P 500 up 0.11% and the Nasdaq 100 down 0.15%, so watch whether the rotation away from tech carries into Friday.
Emerging Asia policy risk: Indonesian stocks plunged after MSCI said the market could be cut from its indices, while China is trying to prop up its own market.
Barclays (BCS) reports earnings on Thursday October 22, the first of your holdings to report this season.

take: Tech selling deepened on Friday and dragged US stocks lower, with the Nasdaq down 2.15% and the S&P 500 down 1.09% as tech fell 3.02%, taking its five-day loss to 7.7%. AI infrastructure names again took the hardest hits, including Nebius (-12.2%) and CoreWeave (-11.9%), extending the AI-related selling of the past week. Money rotated toward energy (+2.52%), utilities (+1.34%) and consumer staples (+1.08%), and energy held up even though WTI crude fell 2.98% to $98.39. Europe followed the US lower on Monday, with the DAX down 1.27% and the FTSE 100 down 1.07%. Asia was mixed: the Kospi rose 1.76% but is still down 9.7% over five days, the Nikkei slipped 0.62%, and Indonesia saw what Reuters called panic selling on an MSCI expulsion threat, likely behind Telkom Indonesia's 13.7% drop.
portfolio: The portfolio fell 0.98%, slightly less than the S&P 500's 1.09%, mostly because of the growth fund SCHG (-2.00%, $-27), along with CRM (-2.45%), AMZN (-1.87%) and GOOGL (-2.47%), as the tech selloff hit growth names. Small gains in AAPL (+0.43%) and MCD (+0.19%) softened the drop.
watch: US futures point to a rebound, with the Nasdaq 100 up 1.08% and the S&P 500 up 0.49%, after last week's tech slide.
Barclays (BCS) reports earnings on Thursday, October 22.
Indonesia's stock and bond selloff over the MSCI expulsion threat, per Reuters and Bloomberg.
deep_dive: The model values DexCom at $28.30 against an $86.04 share price because the reverse DCF says the price implies about 23.4% revenue growth every year for a decade, roughly double the 12.2% analyst estimate for year one, which the model then fades toward 2.5%. The model also keeps the free cash flow margin flat at 15.6% and uses a high 12.13% discount rate, driven by a 1.48 beta and a 5.10% risk-free rate, so the market may be paying for margin expansion or a longer growth runway that a simple DCF ignores. Even the most generous case in the sensitivity table reaches only $35, so the gap is mostly about growth and margin assumptions, and the model is one lens rather than a verdict.

take: US tech bounced on Monday after last week's slide, with tech up 1.36% and the Nasdaq up 1.11%, though tech is still down 5.3% over five days. The S&P 500 gained a smaller 0.41% because the defensive groups that led the recent rotation gave ground, with utilities down 2.01% and real estate down 1.16%, likely pressured as the 10-year yield rose 4 bps to 5.14%. The rebound did not carry into Asia on Tuesday: the Kospi fell 3.73%, extending its five-day loss to 8.0%, and the Nikkei and Hang Seng each dropped about 1.3%, while Telkom Indonesia lost another 5.3% as Indonesia tried to steady its market after the MSCI expulsion threat. Europe also slipped, with the DAX down 0.87% and the Stoxx 600 down 0.70%, and WTI crude fell 3.00% to $100.55.
portfolio: The portfolio rose 0.35%, just behind the S&P 500's 0.41%, as Amazon's 4.98% jump and Schwab's growth fund SCHG (+1.05%, ) rode the rebound in tech and consumer discretionary. Barclays (BCS) fell 2.72% on a weak day for financials, two days before its earnings, which offset much of that gain.
watch: US futures point lower, with the Nasdaq 100 down 0.56%, testing whether Monday's tech bounce holds after Asia's chip-heavy selloff.
Barclays (BCS) reports earnings on Thursday, October 22.
Indonesia's efforts to stabilise its market after the MSCI expulsion threat, which has kept Telkom Indonesia under pressure.

take: The rotation away from tech that has run through this month carried on Tuesday, with health care leading US sectors up 2.37% (up 6.0% over five days) while tech slipped 0.28%, taking its five-day loss to 5.5%. That split left the S&P 500 up 0.28% and the Nasdaq flat at -0.02%, while smaller companies did best, with the Russell 2000 up 1.65%, likely helped by a 2 bp dip in the 10-year yield to 5.12% and gains in rate-sensitive real estate (+1.70%) and utilities (+1.26%). Asia rebounded on Wednesday after last week's chip-driven slide, with the Kospi up 3.29% (still down 4.5% over five days) and the Nikkei up 0.85%, and Telkom Indonesia jumped 11.4% after its recent heavy losses, though the Hang Seng fell 0.90% and Sea Limited dropped 9.1%. Europe followed the firmer tone, with the DAX up 0.73% and the Stoxx 600 up 0.52%, while WTI crude fell another 2.45% to $99.30.
portfolio: The portfolio rose 0.13%, trailing the S&P 500's 0.28%, as gains in McDonald's (+1.59%), the small-cap value fund AVUV (+1.06%), VXUS (+0.54%) and Barclays (+0.72%) fit the day's rotation toward non-tech and smaller stocks. Those were partly offset by Apple (-1.00%) and Alphabet (-1.13%), which together cost about $14 as big tech lagged again.
watch: Barclays (BCS) reports earnings Thursday, a 7% holding and a direct read on a European bank with a large investment bank and prime brokerage business.
Nasdaq 100 futures are up 0.56%, ahead of S&P 500 futures at +0.23%, a sign tech may try to bounce after its five-day slide.
Next Wednesday brings both the Fed rate decision and Alphabet earnings, kicking off a week that includes Amazon and DexCom results.

take: The bigger story is the overnight reversal: after US tech rallied Wednesday, Asia sold off hard on Thursday and US futures now point to a weaker open, with the S&P 500 down 1.05% and the Nasdaq 100 down 1.71% as traders weigh Tesla and Meta earnings. The Kospi fell 3.52%, giving back Wednesday's rebound, the Hang Seng dropped 3.03% (down 5.7% over five days), and the Nikkei lost 2.65%, while Bloomberg says China stocks are nearing a bear market as AI trade and policy hopes fade. In Wednesday's US session, tech led with a 1.67% gain, lifting the Nasdaq 1.05% and the S&P 500 0.58%, helped by moves such as Super Micro's 9.5% jump, though communication services fell 1.11% with Netflix down 5.3% and AT&T down 6.4%. Europe followed Asia lower, with the DAX down 0.91% and the Stoxx 600 down 0.88%, while the yen strengthened about 1% against the dollar, the VIX rose 9.23% to 18.22, and WTI crude climbed 1.78% to $98.88.
portfolio: The portfolio rose just 0.05% against the S&P 500's 0.58%, as gains in Apple (+1.32%) and SCHG (+0.93%) were almost fully offset by DexCom's 6.39% drop, which cost 0.36 points on 2.5 times usual volume, likely tied to attention on its G7 trial publication in NEJM. Alphabet's 1.62% slip, in line with the weak communication sector, also weighed.
watch: Barclays (BCS) reported this morning with EPS of 0.66 versus the 0.67 estimate, a slight miss, though headlines point to higher total income; its average post-earnings move is 2.7%, so watch whether the reaction follows the miss or the income story.
US futures are down 1.05% for the S&P 500 and 1.71% for the Nasdaq 100 as Tesla and Meta results are digested, after Asia's sharp selloff overnight.
DexCom reports on Oct 29 with options implying a 15.5% move, well above its 9.3% average reaction, after this week's slide.

take: An AI-led tech selloff dominated Thursday's US session, with tech down 3.29% and the Nasdaq down 2.60%, likely sparked by Meta, which one headline says fueled an AI meltdown, as chip suppliers such as MACOM (-15.9%) plunged. The S&P 500 fell a smaller 1.21% and the Russell 2000 edged up 0.11% because money again moved toward defensive groups, with consumer staples up 3.31% and utilities up 2.07%. That extends the month-long shift away from tech, helped by a 19 bp drop in the 10-year yield to 4.95% even as WTI crude rose 1.61% to $101.07, a five-month high according to Reuters. Asia was steadier on Friday, with the Hang Seng up 0.69% and the Kospi up 0.30% while Taiwan's market shut for Typhoon Champi, though Europe slipped about 0.5% and the yen firmed 0.77% against the dollar.
portfolio: The portfolio fell 0.89%, less than the S&P 500's 1.21% drop, as losses in SCHG (-0.45 pts) and Amazon (-4.57%) from the tech selloff were partly offset by Salesforce (+3.52%, after agreeing to buy Braze for $5.66B), McDonald's (+2.59%) and Apple (+1.23%). Barclays fell 2.61% after a slight earnings miss, a reaction consistent with the result.
watch: US futures point to a calmer open after Reuters reported the tech selloff relenting, with S&P 500 futures down 0.27% and Nasdaq 100 futures down 0.15%.

Next week stacks up for your holdings: the Fed decides Wednesday alongside Alphabet earnings (options imply a 6.2% move vs a 5.0% average), then Amazon (7.8% implied, matching its average) and Dexcom on Thursday.
Dexcom traded at 3.2x its usual volume with no headline yet, ahead of results where options imply 7.5% against a typical 9.3% move.

take: Friday's US session reversed part of October's defensive rotation: tech rose 0.49% while consumer staples fell 1.92%, communication services fell 1.78% (down 4.4% over five days) and financials fell 1.32%. That left the Nasdaq down just 0.21% and the S&P 500 down 0.52%. Energy was the standout at +2.60% even though WTI crude slipped 2.07% to $101.13, and the 10-year yield rose 3 bps to 4.99%. On Monday Europe firmed, with the DAX up 0.79%, as Bloomberg tied gains to falling oil ahead of big tech earnings. Asia stayed weak outside Hong Kong: the Kospi fell 1.46% (down 5.2% over five days), the Nikkei lost 0.80%, the yen weakened 0.55% to 157.36 per dollar, and the Hang Seng rose 0.51%.
portfolio: The portfolio fell 0.55%, roughly matching the S&P 500's 0.52% drop. The biggest drags were McDonald's (-1.65%), as consumer stocks sold off, and Barclays (-1.23%), which kept sliding after its slight earnings miss on Oct 22, while Apple's small 0.14% dip cushioned the day.
watch: Wednesday brings the Fed decision and Alphabet earnings after the close, with options implying a 6.1% move versus a 5.0% average after its last four reports.
Thursday stacks Amazon (options imply 7.9% versus a 7.8% typical move) and DexCom (13.5% implied versus a 9.3% typical move) on top of Q3 GDP and September PCE inflation.
US futures are flat ahead of the open, while Reuters flags a sharp selloff expected in Brazil's markets after Lula's reelection.
deep_dive: The model values Alphabet at $468.30 versus a $320.21 share price, but today's price implies only about 10.4% revenue growth a year for a decade, while the model starts from analyst estimates of 24% to 25% for the next two years before fading to 2.5%. A simple DCF also holds the 20.8% free cash flow margin flat, so it cannot capture either margin expansion or the risk that heavy spending squeezes cash flow. Every cell in the sensitivity table ($381 to $610) sits above the price, and terminal value makes up 54% of the estimate, so the gap mainly shows how much more cautious the market is about long-run growth and risk than these inputs, rather than proving the stock is cheap.
